name: Endocrine system
description: The endocrine glands and their hormones: the pituitary and hypothalamus, thyroid and parathyroids, adrenals, pancreas, thymus, pineal and gonads, how they are controlled by feedback, and common disorders. Picture questions show the glands, with one part highlighted to name. BodyParts3D has no thyroid, parathyroid or ovary models, so those are text questions.

source.name: Written for Study Buddy. Pictures rendered from BodyParts3D (© The Database Center for Life Science, CC BY-SA 2.1 JP).

questions.prompt: What is the main difference between endocrine and exocrine glands?
answers: Endocrine glands release hormones into the blood; exocrine glands release secretions through ducts
Endocrine glands have no ducts and release hormones into the blood
wrong: Endocrine glands release secretions through ducts onto surfaces
Endocrine glands are only in the brain
questions.explanation: Sweat, saliva and digestive juices are exocrine.

figure.alt: The thymus, pancreas, adrenals and testes in the trunk, in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What is a hormone?
answers: A chemical messenger carried in the blood to target cells
A chemical messenger released into the blood
wrong: A nerve impulse carried along an axon
An enzyme made by the stomach
questions.explanation: Only cells with the right receptor respond.

questions.prompt: Which of these hormones is a steroid, made from cholesterol?
questions.explanation: Steroids cross the cell membrane and act on genes. Peptide hormones bind to receptors on the surface.

questions.prompt: Which gland is called the 'master gland' because it controls many others?
questions.explanation: But the hypothalamus above it controls the pituitary.

questions.prompt: Which structure is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: It links the nervous and endocrine systems. It makes releasing hormones, ADH and oxytocin.

figure.alt: The brain from the left side, with the hypothalamus in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which gland is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: About the size of a pea, in the sella turcica of the sphenoid bone, hanging from the hypothalamus.

figure.alt: The brain from the left side, with the pituitary gland in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which two lobes does the pituitary gland have?
questions.explanation: The anterior lobe makes its own hormones. The posterior lobe only stores and releases those made in the hypothalamus.

figure.alt: The brain from the left side, with the pituitary gland in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which bone holds the pituitary gland in a hollow called the sella turcica?
questions.explanation: Its name means 'Turkish saddle'.

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT released by the anterior pituitary?
questions.explanation: ADH and oxytocin are made in the hypothalamus and released from the posterior pituitary.

questions.prompt: Which anterior pituitary hormone makes children grow, by acting on bone and liver?
questions.explanation: Too much in a child gives gigantism; in an adult, acromegaly.

questions.prompt: Which pituitary hormone makes the thyroid release thyroid hormones?
Which pituitary hormone makes the adrenal cortex release cortisol?
Which pituitary hormone makes the breast produce milk?
Which posterior pituitary hormone makes the uterus contract in labour and milk flow from the breast?
Which posterior pituitary hormone makes the kidney keep water?
questions.explanation: Lack of it causes diabetes insipidus, with a lot of dilute urine.

questions.prompt: How do hypothalamic releasing hormones reach the anterior pituitary?
answers: Through a small portal system of blood vessels
In the hypophyseal portal blood vessels
questions.explanation: The posterior pituitary, in contrast, is joined to the hypothalamus by nerve fibres.

questions.prompt: Which gland is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: A tiny gland above the midbrain, which makes melatonin.

figure.alt: The brain from the left side, with the pineal gland in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which hormone, made by the pineal gland mostly at night, helps set the sleep rhythm?
questions.explanation: Light on the retina switches it off.

questions.prompt: Where is the thyroid gland?
answers: In the front of the neck, on either side of the trachea below the larynx
In the neck, in front of the trachea
wrong: At the base of the brain
questions.explanation: It has two lobes joined by a narrow isthmus, and weighs about 25 g. There is no model of it in the picture set.

questions.prompt: Which two main hormones does the thyroid release?
questions.explanation: They set the body's metabolic rate.

questions.prompt: Which mineral is needed to make thyroid hormones?
questions.explanation: Lack of it makes the thyroid swell, which is called a goitre.

questions.prompt: Which hormone from the thyroid's C cells lowers the blood calcium?
How many parathyroid glands are there, and where?
answers: Usually four, on the back of the thyroid
wrong: Two, on top of the kidneys
One, in front of the trachea
questions.explanation: They make parathyroid hormone (PTH), which raises the blood calcium.

questions.prompt: Which hormone raises the blood calcium by acting on bone, kidney and gut?
questions.explanation: The kidney turns vitamin D into calcitriol under its influence, so more calcium is absorbed.

questions.prompt: Which glands are highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: One sits on top of each kidney, like a cap.

figure.alt: The adrenal glands, in red, above the kidneys
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What are the two main parts of an adrenal gland?
questions.explanation: The outer cortex makes steroids. The inner medulla makes adrenaline.

figure.alt: The adrenal glands, in red, above the kidneys
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which adrenal cortex hormone helps the body cope with long-term stress, raising blood glucose and suppressing inflammation?
questions.explanation: Controlled by ACTH from the pituitary.

questions.prompt: Which adrenal cortex hormone makes the kidney keep sodium?
Which hormone from the adrenal medulla prepares the body for 'fight or flight'?
questions.explanation: It speeds the heart and widens the airways. It is released when the sympathetic nerves fire.

questions.prompt: Which organ is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: It lies behind the stomach, and is both an exocrine and an endocrine gland.

figure.alt: The pancreas, in red, with the duodenum and spleen
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What are the clusters of endocrine cells in the pancreas called?
questions.explanation: They make up only about 1 to 2% of the pancreas.

questions.prompt: Which pancreatic hormone, made by beta cells, lowers the blood glucose?
Which pancreatic hormone, made by alpha cells, raises the blood glucose?
questions.explanation: It makes the liver break down glycogen.

questions.prompt: Which gland is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: It lies in the chest behind the sternum. It is large in children and shrinks in adults.

figure.alt: The thymus behind the sternum, in red, with the rib cage drawn see-through
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What is the thymus for?
answers: It is where T cells mature
wrong: It makes red blood cells in adults
questions.explanation: It also makes the hormone thymosin.

questions.prompt: Which organs are highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: As well as making sperm, they make testosterone.

figure.alt: The testes in the scrotum, in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which hormones do the ovaries make?
questions.explanation: FSH and LH come from the pituitary.

questions.prompt: Which two hormones does the kidney make?
questions.explanation: It also activates vitamin D.

questions.prompt: Which hormone does the heart release when its atria are stretched, to lower blood volume?
questions.explanation: It makes the kidneys lose sodium and water.

questions.prompt: Which hormone, made in the stomach, makes you feel hungry?
questions.explanation: Leptin, from fat cells, does the opposite.

questions.prompt: Which hormone from fat cells tells the brain that there are energy stores?
Which hormone from the stomach makes it release acid?
Which hormone from the duodenum makes the gallbladder contract and the pancreas release enzymes?
What kind of control keeps most hormone levels steady?
questions.explanation: A rise in the hormone's effect shuts off its release. Oxytocin in labour is a rare example of positive feedback.

questions.prompt: In the control of the thyroid, which is the right order?
answers: TRH, TSH, then T3 and T4
questions.explanation: T3 and T4 then feed back to shut off TRH and TSH.

questions.prompt: After a meal, which hormone makes the liver and muscle store glucose as glycogen?
questions.explanation: Between meals glucagon does the opposite.

questions.prompt: What is the problem in type 1 diabetes?
answers: The immune system destroys the beta cells, so there is no insulin
wrong: The cells do not respond to insulin
The pancreas makes too much insulin
The liver makes too much glucagon
questions.explanation: It usually starts in childhood and needs insulin injections.

questions.prompt: What is the main problem in type 2 diabetes?
answers: The cells respond poorly to insulin (insulin resistance)
wrong: The beta cells are destroyed by the immune system
questions.explanation: It is linked with obesity, and usually starts in adults.

questions.prompt: Which group of symptoms is typical of diabetes?
answers: Thirst, passing a lot of urine, tiredness, weight loss
wrong: Slow heart rate and weight gain
questions.explanation: The high blood glucose spills into the urine and drags water with it.

questions.prompt: Which set of signs goes with an overactive thyroid (hyperthyroidism, as in Graves' disease)?
answers: Weight loss, fast heart, sweating, heat intolerance, tremor
Weight loss, fast heartbeat, heat intolerance
wrong: Weight gain, slow heart, cold intolerance, tiredness
Moon face, thin skin, high blood pressure

questions.prompt: Which set of signs goes with an underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism)?
answers: Weight gain, slow heart, cold intolerance, tiredness
wrong: Weight loss, fast heart, heat intolerance, tremor
High blood pressure and moon face
questions.explanation: In infants, untreated, it causes cretinism (congenital hypothyroidism), which is now found by newborn screening.

questions.prompt: What is a swelling of the thyroid called?
questions.explanation: Most often from a lack of iodine.

questions.prompt: Which condition comes from too much cortisol, with a round face, thin skin and high blood pressure?
Which condition comes from too little cortisol and aldosterone, with weakness, low blood pressure and dark skin?
questions.explanation: The dark skin is from high ACTH, which acts on melanocytes.

questions.prompt: What happens when an adult makes too much growth hormone?
answers: Acromegaly: the hands, feet and face grow bigger
questions.explanation: Usually from a pituitary tumour. In a child, with the growth plates still open, it gives gigantism.

questions.prompt: Lack of which hormone causes diabetes insipidus, with large amounts of dilute urine?
questions.explanation: It has nothing to do with blood sugar.

questions.prompt: Overactive parathyroid glands cause which change in the blood?
questions.explanation: 'Stones, bones, groans and moans': kidney stones, bone pain, abdominal pain and low mood.

questions.prompt: What is the main controller of the blood calcium level?
questions.explanation: With calcitonin and vitamin D helping.

questions.prompt: What decides which cells respond to a hormone?
answers: Whether they have receptors for it
wrong: How close they are to the gland
Whether they have a nerve supply

questions.prompt: Which part of the nervous system is linked to the adrenal medulla?
questions.explanation: Its cells are like modified sympathetic neurons.

questions.prompt: Where in the hypothalamus is the body's main clock?
questions.explanation: It sits above the optic chiasm and gets light signals from the eyes.
